back: A construct where a condition (TRUE or FALSE) decides which statements run next.

IF condition
    THEN
        statements
    ELSE
        statements
ENDIF

CASE OF Variable
    value1 : statement
    value2 : statement
    OTHERWISE statement
ENDCASE
With >= tests, check the highest boundary first; otherwise high values stop at a lower branch.
CASE: one variable against single values (menus). IF: ranges, several variables, AND/OR conditions.
Cases are tested in order; the first match runs and control passes to after ENDCASE.
Separate IFs are all tested, so several can run. Use ELSE / nesting when only one outcome may apply.
Test on and either side of each boundary (e.g. 49, 50, 74, 75) to catch > / >= errors.
